text:
𝗢𝗻𝗲 𝗰𝗮𝗻'𝘁 𝗯𝗲 𝗮 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗲 𝗷𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝗯𝗲𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲.🚫

 This might be my biggest insight of the year.

 I thought I was a pretty good leader. Using progressive practices, reading the right books, and having the right conversations. And then I caught myself on something so simple —𝗜 𝘄𝗮𝘀 𝗷𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝘀. And I realized I still have a long way to go.

 Here's what happened. 👇

 I was watching some documentaries about the opioid crisis in the US. If you haven't followed this, pharmaceutical companies convinced doctors that opioid painkillers weren't addictive. Millions of people got hooked on what was essentially legal heroin.

 Complicated topic. Not black and white. But there was this one idea that stuck with me: we cannot judge those who are fighting addiction or pain because we can't imagine what they're living through. Literally.

 And somewhere in that moment, I started thinking about leadership.

 Recently, we gathered with our Speed and Function leadership team offline. During one of the meetings, my phone started dying, and the red battery indicator popped up. I noticed our founder Nick wincing. Then he reaches over, pulls out a power bank, plugs my phone in, and literally exhales with relief. 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁'𝘀 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝗿𝗲𝗱 — the phone has to be charged.

 My first instinct? 𝘞𝘩𝘺 𝘥𝘰𝘦𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘢𝘵𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘵𝘰 𝘺𝘰𝘶? 𝘐𝘵'𝘴 𝘫𝘶𝘴𝘵 𝘢 𝘣𝘢𝘵𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘺.

 And that's when it hit me. 💡 My reaction — 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁'𝘀 𝗷𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁. I was evaluating his experience through my own lens. I've never felt what he feels when he sees that red bar. I simply don't have access to that experience.

 I thought I wasn't judging before. Until I realized — yeah, that's exactly what I was doing.

 I wasn't the leader I thought I was.

 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 𝗶𝘀 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁. 𝗜𝘁 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀 𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘆 𝗼𝗻 𝗽𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗿. 𝗜𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗹𝗶𝗳𝗲, 𝗶𝘁'𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗯𝗹𝘆 𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱.

 So now I try to follow a simpler formula: understand that you won't understand. Not "try harder to understand." Not "put yourself in their shoes." Just accept that their shoes don't fit your feet.

 I'll never be a leader who knows everything. It's an endless path. And right now, there are things I still don't know and don't understand. That's just where I am.

 Btw, after this story with the dying battery, my relationship with our founder — which was already good — became even better. 🤝 And I believe this has a positive impact on our business. When you stop judging and start accepting, things just work smoother.
